title: Chapter 1: The Dinner Table
staging: One long kitchen table stays center stage for the whole act. It becomes a farmhouse supper table, a job-site bench, a fair counter, a church pew rail and, at last, the Pattersons' kitchen. Downstage left: a stool and a small reading stand for KAMBRIA, who tells this part of the story and never fully leaves the stage. The back wall takes projections: verses, dates, a drawing.
cast: Angela's closest friend. Tells this part of the story from the stool, and steps into it when it reaches her.
Seen at 10, 18, 23 and in his forties. Says little; his hands are always busy.
His second wife. Talks with her hands. Leaves her hand open on the table at every supper.
Ezra's son. Three at the fair, sixteen in the kitchen. A cello never far off.
Ezra and Angela's daughter. Three at her birthday, four in the kitchen. Two puffs, yellow ribbons.
Angela's father. Upright, sparing with words, missing nothing.
Angela's mother. Cupcakes, one candle, every time.
Ezra's father. Gray suit on Sunday. Silent, seen in memory.
Ezra's first wife. Silent; a phone in her hand.
Ezra's friend from boyhood. Loud. Silent in this chapter.
NOAH, HIS SONS, NEIGHBORS, A YOUNG MAN
MR. ODELL, WALT SIMMONS, CHURCH WOMEN, PARTY GUESTS, GIRLFRIENDS, A VENDOR

scenes.title: Opening
scenes.setting: Dark stage. The long table under a single hanging lamp, set for no one.

scenes.title: The Hill
scenes.setting: The ancient world. A slope upstage right, half-built ribs of a great hull against the sky.

scenes.title: Cedar Hollow
scenes.setting: Rural Maryland, decades earlier. A farmhouse on Old Ferry Road; the long table is its supper table.

scenes.title: Two Quiet People
scenes.setting: A job site, a backyard wedding, a doorway, a crowded house party in Brookland, a truck cab, a kitchen counter. Summer 2011.

scenes.title: The Fair
scenes.setting: A county fair, the third week of August. Ninety-four degrees.

scenes.title: Thanksgiving
scenes.setting: Ezra's one-bedroom apartment, then the parking lot outside it, that November.

scenes.title: Twelfth Street
scenes.setting: A small brick church in June; then the gutted house in Brookland and its back lot.

scenes.title: The Good Years
scenes.setting: The rebuilt house over several years: the yard, the studio, a park, the fair, the supper table.

scenes.title: The Blessing
scenes.setting: A church fellowship hall; then the Pattersons' kitchen on Thursdays; then Mia's third birthday.

scenes.title: The Lab
scenes.setting: Two years before the trumpet. A government building with no windows.

scenes.title: Twelfth Street, Thursday
scenes.setting: Brookland, a quarter to seven on a warm Thursday evening.

scenes.title: Supper
scenes.setting: The Pattersons' kitchen. Steam, three pans, a side door and a screen door to the yard.

scenes.title: The Word
scenes.setting: The same kitchen, later. The table cleared for study.

scenes.title: The Doomsday Club
scenes.setting: The same kitchen. The studio glows across the yard.

scenes.title: The Red Sky
scenes.setting: The same kitchen, an hour past Mia's bedtime.

scenes.title: The Lump
scenes.setting: The same kitchen. Only the lamp over the table and the light from the stove clock.

scenes.title: The Stairwell
scenes.setting: The next afternoon. A concrete stairwell between the third and fourth floors of the lab building.

scenes.title: For Ezra
scenes.setting: That same night. The Pattersons' kitchen, everyone else asleep.

dirs.-1: House lights down. KAMBRIA enters in a coat, sits on the stool, opens a red spiral notebook on the stand, and gives the act.
dirs.0: Kambria gives the chapter title to the house.
dirs.1: The back wall: HEBREWS 11:7, appearing a line at a time under her voice.
dirs.2: The wall changes to one Greek word and its number, G5537.
dirs.3: Light finds the hill. NOAH, gray-bearded, works a beam with an adze. HIS SONS drag timber up the slope. Lower down, NEIGHBORS lounge on the grass with wine jars. A YOUNG MAN cups his hands and shouts up at the old man; the slope laughs. Noah wipes his brow, takes up the adze again, and keeps at it as the light leaves him.
dirs.5: The back wall: LONG BEFORE THE TRUMPET.
dirs.6: Gravel crunches underfoot. YOUNG EZRA (10) comes on with a creek stone tied to a length of twine and holds it against a doorframe, watching it settle.
dirs.8: CALVIN PATTERSON enters in a gray suit, working a receiving line of hands that are not there, smiling at every one. LORETTA follows, nodding to church women we cannot see.
dirs.9: Calvin hangs the suit coat on a door upstage and stops smiling. He takes the head of the table. Loretta serves. Young Ezra sits. Nobody speaks. Boots drop in the hall; a television glow upstage cuts out. Loretta exits to bed. Calvin reaches into the high cabinet for a bottle. Later, alone, Loretta pins a calendar over a dark hole in the plaster.
dirs.10: Young Ezra at the table, motionless.
dirs.11: Loretta alone on a pew bench, a Bible in her lap. Ezra, older, lifts keys from a hook and leaves by the other side.
dirs.12: EZRA (18) swings into the bed of a pickup with a crew. A year passes in a light shift: ELIJAH BROOKS vaults in after him, talking, and knocks a level off the tailgate. Ezra picks it up and hands it back.
dirs.14: Sawhorses, a set of plans held flat by a brick. MICHELLE, clipboard in hand, taps the plans and then her watch. EZRA (23), a hammer on his belt, listens. He says something we do not hear. She laughs.
dirs.15: A string of bulbs over a backyard; a few folding chairs. Michelle and Ezra stand together under it. A bassinet is set down at the table.
dirs.16: The doorway. Michelle, a rolling suitcase at her heel, hands toddler JALEN to Ezra and goes. She comes back; he hands the boy over. Again, quicker each time, neither looking up. A phone lights on the table and rings out.
dirs.17: Music thuds through a wall. Bodies fill a narrow living room. ELIJAH steers Ezra and Michelle in. Michelle heads straight for the kitchen with her phone at her ear. Ezra takes a red cup and plants himself by the back door.
dirs.18: The crowd thins in front of him.
dirs.19: ANGELA, pencil skirt and cardigan, center, mid-story, her hands carrying half of it. A GIRLFRIEND at each elbow. She feels him looking and turns. Neither looks away.
dirs.20: Ezra's thumb finds his wedding band and turns it.
dirs.21: He stays at the door. Angela, talking to a man, holds up three fingers and laughs with her whole face.
dirs.22: Two chairs side by side for the truck cab. Michelle types on her phone. Ezra drives. Headlights slide over both of them.
dirs.23: Morning. A folded note propped against the coffee maker. Ezra reads it. JALEN (3), in pajamas, holds on to his leg.
dirs.25: Hard white light. The tinny loop of a carousel organ. A hand-lettered sign: FRIED DOUGH. EZRA carries JALEN (3) on his hip.
dirs.26: The carousel turns; they ride it, then again. Something large snorts offstage. A dim barn: cages stacked on both sides. Jalen asleep on Ezra's shoulder. Ezra stands in the aisle and does not move.
dirs.27: Ezra steps out into the glare.
dirs.28: ANGELA, sundress and straw hat, in line at the window between two GIRLFRIENDS who talk at once. Her eyes go to him, to the sleeping boy, to his bare left hand. She lets the question go unasked.
dirs.37: Angela turns to the window and lifts one finger to the VENDOR. A paper plate comes out piled white with sugar; she sets it in Ezra's free hand.
dirs.41: Ezra fishes for his wallet one-handed. Jalen wakes, lunges with both fists; sugar everywhere. Angela laughs.
dirs.44: Lamp light, a crowded table, too many chairs for one small room. On the back wall, a snow-bound lakeshore.
dirs.45: JOE walks the apartment upright and silent and runs a thumbnail down the seam of a bookshelf. PAT sets down chocolate cupcakes with sprinkles and pushes one candle into the middle. JALEN (3) blows it out. Pat relights it. He blows again.
dirs.46: Night. One lamppost, a sedan. Joe at the driver's door, keys in hand, facing Ezra.
dirs.48: Joe nods once, gets in, and the headlights swing away.
dirs.50: Two short rows of pews. JALEN (4) carries a ring pillow down the aisle and drops it; picks it up; drops it again. PAT dabs her eyes. JOE walks ANGELA down, sets her hand in Ezra's, and is slow to let go.
dirs.51: Ezra turns and looks out at the pews, to an empty place on the groom's side. He turns back.
dirs.52: Bare studs. A tarp for a roof, sky showing through. Behind it a long lot of weeds and glass. Ezra hands a set of truck keys offstage.
dirs.54: Ezra sets a stair tread. Angela rolls paint up a wall. JALEN (5) hammers nails crooked into a scrap of two-by-four, humming.
dirs.55: Spring. EZRA down in a trench in the back lot, red clay to his knees, soaked through. ANGELA comes down the back step with two glasses of iced tea and sits.
dirs.56: He stops and leans on the shovel.
dirs.58: Angela sets the glasses on the step and walks into the mud in her good sneakers.
dirs.62: JALEN (9) carries in a battered cello case. At the far end of the yard Ezra frames a small studio; inside it, the boy plays with the windows open. Across the street, WALT SIMMONS on his porch, newspaper up.
dirs.63: A newborn: MIA. PAT at the stove, every burner going. JOE on the back step with the baby in his arms, a long time. He hands her to Ezra and turns his face away.
dirs.64: A swing set: Ezra pushing. Angela on a blanket with a book. Jalen running scales under a tree. Then the fair once more: one paper plate, two halves, and Angela takes the sweeter one.
dirs.65: Supper. Angela bows her head and lays her left hand open on the cloth beside Ezra's plate. Jalen takes her right. Ezra's hand stays on his fork.
dirs.67: Angela alone at the table, a pen between her teeth, notebooks in four colors fanned out and a concordance open that takes both hands to lift. Upstage, a church basement: folding chairs and FOURTEEN WOMEN.
dirs.68: A young woman in a lab coat slips into the back row: KAMBRIA, years younger. From the stool, the storyteller watches herself sit down.
dirs.69: Week by week the chairs empty until only Angela and the young Kambria are left. Together they carry the notebooks out of the basement and into Angela's kitchen.
dirs.71: EZRA comes in from work, finds the two heads bent over the Hebrew, and stops in the doorway.
dirs.72: Ezra and ELIJAH at a bar rail with two bottles. Then the bedroom: Ezra on his side, eyes shut, as Angela reaches for him.
dirs.73: Two in the morning. Only the stove hood light. Angela at the table, eyes closed, lips moving. Ezra in the doorway with a glass of water hears his own name.
dirs.74: Upstage, faint: CALVIN at the deacons' table in the gray suit, one hand raised. YOUNG EZRA (6) in the front pew, rigid.
dirs.75: The kitchen. MIA (3) kneeling on a chair. PAT sets down chocolate cupcakes with sprinkles, one candle lit. JOE and JALEN around the table. Angela touches Ezra's arm.
dirs.77: Nobody moves. The candle burns down.
dirs.78: Behind Ezra, Calvin's shape, close, and gone.
dirs.82: Night. The back step. Ezra alone. JOE comes out, hands in his pockets, and stands beside him.
dirs.83: Joe goes in. The screen door clicks shut.
dirs.85: The back wall: TWO YEARS BEFORE THE TRUMPET.
dirs.86: White light, no windows. Kambria rises from the stool, takes a lab coat from the stand and steps into the story. From here she narrates from inside it.
dirs.87: A break room table with a newspaper. Kambria reads the headline and laughs out loud. She reads on and stops laughing. She cuts the page free and folds it into her coat pocket.
dirs.88: At the bench: racks of sample tubes, a printout of DNA bands.
dirs.89: She frowns at a monitor, types, and sends.
dirs.90: Dusk. A row of porch-front houses, small gardens. A speaker on a porch rail sends a song over the roofs; a church bell starts to ring. MR. ODELL in a lawn chair two doors down. Kambria parks and gets out. He lifts two fingers from the armrest. She lifts two back.
dirs.91: The long table is the Pattersons' kitchen now. Three pans steam on the stove; a skillet spits. ANGELA works them with a dish towel over one shoulder and a wooden spoon in her hand. Kambria comes in through the side door.
dirs.99: MIA (4), two puffs tied with yellow ribbons, kneels on a chair over a coloring page with a purple crayon.
dirs.105: The screen door slaps. JALEN (16), headphones around his neck, kisses his mother's cheek, steals a pierogi out of the skillet and ducks the spoon.
dirs.113: Jalen loads a plate and goes out the back. The screen door slaps twice. Offstage, out in the yard, a cello starts.
dirs.114: They eat standing at the counter. Angela moves food around her plate. Twice her left hand drifts to her side and away.
dirs.120: Plates stacked in the rack. Angela carries Mia off and comes back. The two women sit across the table: two cooling mugs, two worn Bibles, notebooks in blue, red, green and gold.
dirs.125: Between the Bibles, the concordance, its spine mended with packing tape.
dirs.126: Angela's finger on a verse. Kambria runs down the columns at the back of the concordance.
dirs.130: Angela writes small in her margin, then looks through the doorway at the couch in the next room. Empty.
dirs.133: Kambria smooths a newspaper clipping flat on the red notebook.
dirs.139: Kambria lays the ark clipping on the table. The back wall shows it: a long, boat-shaped hill under snow.
dirs.142: On the windowsill a small radio murmurs a news report. Kambria writes in the margin. Her eyes go to the dent in the couch cushion.
dirs.144: EZRA, boots caked in mud, a tool belt slung low, drywall dust in his hair.
dirs.145: He kicks his boots off by the door and heads for the refrigerator.
dirs.146: Angela tips her face up. He kisses her forehead.
dirs.151: He takes a beer and lets the refrigerator door swing shut hard. Out in the yard, the cello: one long low note.
dirs.152: Ezra at the window over the sink. Across the yard the studio windows glow amber. In that light, a memory: Ezra and an eleven-year-old JALEN raising a wall, Angela holding the level; the two of them at the breaker, every light coming on at once.
dirs.153: He turns away from the window.
dirs.156: Across the back of the stage, MR. HART, a viola case in hand, pauses to fix a small boy's bow hold, and moves on.
dirs.162: Light catches the watch on Ezra's wrist. Its hands do not move.
dirs.169: MIA in the doorway in pajamas, a sheet of paper pressed to her chest.
dirs.172: She crosses the linoleum and lays the drawing on the red notebook.
dirs.173: The drawing fills the back wall: a house with a crooked porch light, a sky colored red from edge to edge, and in the middle of it a small yellow circle pouring out light.
dirs.178: She points at a small brown shape in the front window.
dirs.179: Overhead, water rushes through the pipes.
dirs.180: Angela scoops Mia up and carries her off.
dirs.181: Angela returns and sits. She finds her place and reads aloud.
dirs.185: She reaches across the notebooks and the drawing and takes both of Kambria's hands.
dirs.190: She draws Kambria's fingers to her own side, under her left arm.
dirs.197: Kambria comes around the table and kneels. Angela bends forward into her arms.
dirs.202: The clock over the stove ticks.
dirs.205: They join hands across the notebooks and bow their heads.
dirs.209: Concrete steps, a steel rail. Kambria in her lab coat. Her phone buzzes.
dirs.210: The text appears on the back wall.
dirs.211: She sits on a step, takes out the gold notebook, writes a name, then the date.
dirs.212: Dark kitchen, the lamp over the table the only light. Angela alone. She peels the wrapper off a plain black notebook.
dirs.213: She writes on the cover and waits for the ink.
dirs.214: Two words on the back wall. She closes the notebook. Blackout.
